chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, and Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all together from al-Wassa, from Ahmad ibn A'idh, from Abu Khadija, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
He does not eat, nor anyone from his family, from the 'Aqeeqa.
He said: And for the midwife is one-third of the 'Aqeeqa. So if the midwife was the mother of the man, or among his family members, then she is not entitled to anything from it.
And it should be made into parts, then cooked, and distributed, and it is not given except to the people of Wilayah.
And he said: Everyone eats from the 'Aqeeqa except the mother.

key_terms.أَهْلِ الْوَلَايَةِ: Ahl al-Wilayah: The people of guardianship/authority, often referring to the Imams or their close associates
key_terms.الْأُمَّ: Al-Umm: The mother of the newborn
key_terms.الْعَقِيقَةِ: Aqeeqa: The sacrificial animal offered for a newborn child

ai.seo_question: Who is entitled to eat from the Aqeeqa sacrifice according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the specific distribution of the 'Aqeeqa sacrifice, emphasizing that the father and his dependents are excluded to prevent self-enrichment, while the midwife receives a fixed one-third share unless she is a dependent. The meat is prepared and distributed exclusively to the 'Ahl al-Wilayah, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the spiritual and social authority of the Imams and their followers in communal religious acts.
